newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: A sharply weaker start on Wall Street on Friday knocked South African stocks off kilter, taking key indices to the day's lowest levels at the close.
Dealers said stocks took fright as the Dow Jones industrial index shed over one percent early in its trading session after the release of U.S. economic data pointing to a strong economy.
This was seen heightening the likelihood of another interest rate hike there.
"The fact that the figures are showing inflationary pressures has obviously dented sentiment in the (United) States. Bonds have weakened and shares are down," a share dealer said.
"That has given our market a bit of a knock."
U.S. figures released earlier showed a 0.4 percent jump in core producer inflation in March and a 0.2 percent increase in retail sales in the same month.
The Federal Reserve last hiked interest rates by 0.25 of a percentage point on March 25 this year.
South Africa's industrial index lost 29.4 points to 8,214.3, dragging the all-share index of 23.1 points to 7,022.0.
Heavyweight stocks turned losers after hovering steady for most of the session with SAB off 25 cents at 134.25 rand, Remgro ditching 75 cents to 44.50 and RMB Holdings dumping 200 cents to 107 rand.
On the gold board, stocks were largely mixed, drooping slightly towards the finish in sympathy with industrials and as bullion slipped below the $348 level.
Vaal Reefs added six rand to 284 rand but Eastvaal slipped 10 cents to 596 cents. The 100 percent gold index shed 4.1 points to 1,306.8.
"Golds were pretty featureless and are likely to stay that way until the quarterlies come out or there is a major move on bullion," a trader said.
First quarter results for the gold mining industry start being reported next week, with Gold Fields kicking off on Thursday.

Dealers said market turnover was average at around 665 million rand, but had once again been characterised by a few major deals. These included Tempora which traded over 2.3 million shares and Malbak which saw a few corporate finance deals.

Traders said stocks would eye Wall Street's performance tonight with concerns on a U.S. rate hike hanging over the market next week. However, continued underlying demand was seen helping shares weather heavy losses in the U.S.
"I think it will continue to drift around, it might come up a bit, but more likely it will be slightly softer," said Willi Jonker, executive director of portfolio management at Norwich Investments.
The equity futures market was also spooked by the inflationary U.S. numbers later on Friday after a firmer start as players were caught short.
All eyes would turn to the U.S. next week, dealers said.
"We will be economic data-watching," one said.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,460/70 from 6,489, the industrial contract at 8,013/18 from 8,036 and the gold June at 915/25 from 925.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
